How to use this report

This report highlights Trump’s Truth Social posts that have most alienated his base, and their verbatim responses to him. These are the posts with the highest comments-to-like ratio for the selected window, meaning that proportionally more people respond to the post than like it. In some cases a high ratio is from Trump asking a question, so those posts are excluded. In most (but not all!) of the remaining cases, the response ratio is high because folks had an important concern.

Each entry can be expanded to see both the text and images associated with the post and the five highest-engagement text comments on that post. In the cases of contentious posts, the comments are typically the most unvarnished and heavily endorsed voices of his supporters’ opposition to that post. Comments in favor of Trump on these posts are likely to be bot-promoted; comments critical of Trump are almost certainly real humans.

How these numbers are counted
  • Ratio is defined as replies per 10 likes.
  • Engagement numbers are a snapshot and show the updated date.
  • Top text replies are defined as "likes + retruths". Replies with images are excluded, as they are usually propaganda meme spam.
  • All times are in EST.
  • Polls and direct questions are excluded. A question inside a longer post is kept.
  • Data covers original posts only, excluding endorsements and retruths.
Truth Social user profile

TruthSocial users skew heavily male (68%, Statistica), and much older than other social media platforms. SimilarWeb estimates that 51% of the TruthSocial user base is above 45 years old, with only 10% below the age of 24. Other estimates show an even older skew of 65% of users above the age of 55 (GWS Magnify).

In 2026, Pew found that only 4% of U.S. adults used Truth Social. Republicans were seven times as likely as Democrats to use it, 7% versus 1%. These responses therefore come from a small, older, mostly male and overwhelmingly Republican political environment.
